 Order

The appellant has filed this Misc. Appeal filed under Section 173(1) of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 being aggrieved by the award dated 27.04.2016 passed by the IV Additional Member, Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Khargone (M.P.) in Claim Case No.03/2014, whereby challenging the quantum of compensation only on the grounds of incorrect assessment of income and failure to add future prospects.

entities.text: IV Additional Member, Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Khargone (M.P.)
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 2. Short facts of the case are that the on 01.05.2012 at around 1:15 PM, appellant along with his friend Rameshwar was going on his motorcycle bearing registration MP-10-MD-5675.

When they reached near Barod Fata Petrol Pump on Khargone-Julvaniya Road, a vehicle (407) bearing registration MP-41-GA-0436 driven in a rash and negligent manner, collided with the motorcycle of the appellant, resulting in grievous injuries to the NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2025:MPHC-IND:28762 2 MA-1328-2016 appellant.
Subsequently, the appellant filed a claim petition under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act before the Claims Tribunal claiming compensation for the injuries sustained in the aforesaid accident.
The Claims Tribunal after recording the evidence assessed the total compensation at Rs.3,37,000/-.
3. Learned counsel for the appellant submits that the Claims Tribunal erred in assessing the income of the appellant.

It was submitted before the Claims Tribunal that the appellate was earning Rs.200/- per day; however, the Claims Tribunal has taken his income as Rs.3,000/- per month on a notional basis, which is even below the minimum wages prescribed for an unskilled labourer.
It is further submitted that no addition under the head of future prospects has been made.

Accordingly,
learned counsel prays for enhancement of compensation.

1 4.

Per contra, learned counsel for the Insurance Company submits that there was no proper pleading regarding the income of the appellant, therefore, the Claims Tribunal has rightly assessed the income on a notional basis.
He thus prays for dismissal of the appeal.

5. Heard learned counsel for the respective parties and perused the record.
6.
From perusal of the record of the Claims Tribunal, it appears that there was no material on record to support the claim that the appellant was earning Rs.200/- per day.
As such, the Claims Tribunal rightly discarded this claim.

However, it is equally true that the minimum wages as on the date of the accident i.e. 01.05.2012 for an unskilled labourer were Rs.4,470/- per NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-IND:28762 3 MA-1328-2016 month, which in the considered view of this Court should be taken as the income of the appellant.

7. In view of the law laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of National Insurance Company Ltd. vs. Pranay Sethi, reported in 2017 ACJ 2700, a 40% addition is to be made to the income of the deceased, considering that he was around 19 years of age.

entities.text: National Insurance Company Ltd. vs. Pranay Sethi, reported in 2017 ACJ 2700
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: As such, the total compensation for loss of earning capacity now amounts to Rs.7,21,224/-.
After deducting the awarded already under this head i.e. Rs.3,24,000/-, the enhanced compensation payable to the appellate comes to Rs.3,97,224/-.
This amount shall be paid over and above the amount already awarded with an interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of filing of the claim petition.
8. It is seen from the record that the appeal has been valued at Rs.11,000/-.
The appellant is directed to deposit the deficit court fee within a period of four weeks from today.
9. With the aforesaid, the present appeal stands disposed off.
Certified copy as per rules.

(PAVAN KUMAR DWIVEDI) JUDGE Anushree Prakash vs Mahendra on 27 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/191639546/
